# START WEB AND SERVER

human.json holds:
    human files,
    abstraction paths
    project id
abstraction_<path>.json has:
    file path,
    every abstraction text, pins, line numbers

[web is in ~/.human](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:from ~/.human/web.html)


if human init or human serve ran:
    if human init: [deletes the map in human/ of a file that is not on disk](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:human init).
    if server not started, start the serve
    if server already runs on port:
        if same machine, [send the project to the already running server](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:give the server the project).


    if port already in use, stop and print reason
    if server doesn't answer in ten seconds: stop and print log.
    if human/human.json has a project with no id: stop and print the reason
    
    find the folder that holds human/human.json, send to human server

    in the project the commands is run:
        if [maps named explanation_](compiler/cli/human/helpers.py:migrate),: become abstraction_    
        if old human/project.json: becomes a human file named after the project folder. 

    printing the localhost web link
    [if not windows: bind tailnet](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:cmd_serve), [print the tailnet line](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:print_links).


if link to web clicked and project id not in [the list of projects in ~/.human/projects.json](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:read the list of projects): show error


while server running:
    [server writes to human/server/serve.log](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:cmd_serve)
    keeps open the conection for the next request and closes it after 30 seconds if no request
    if the browser allows it, sends file info compressed to browser
 
    server keeps list of files on memory with version code

    every 5 seconds the web requests for human.json and sends version code:
        checks folders with stamp changed
        if liste of file changed:
            server reads human.json
            updates it with the files and human files that are on disk
            answers the whole file list

            if new list empty: web keeps tree
            if file is the same: web shows the same file
            if new or deleted file:
                web updates tree
                if selected file deleted: web shows first file open
            if edited file:
                web keeps selected file open


# WEB LOADS

every five seconds, at the same time:
    the page asks for human.json
    if first time, ask the server once for maps:
        request abstraction_<name>.json of every file in the map folder. 
        read the file path,
        server ignores maps with no files and that can't be opened as JSON.
    [ask the server for a tip](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:loadTip)

if tip:
    if tip names a file,
        open that file first.
        a green hand-drawn font arrow with "This is human code" floats at the right of the first line of the draft.
    if tip points at a line of an abstraction:
        abstraction opens and the page scrolls the line to a third of the screen.
        light it with a slow yellow glow; 
        a green hand-drawn arrow with "This is a new change" floats up and down at the right of the line;    
    the green compile button glows 
if click away or compiled, the tip goes away.

[every three seconds](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:pollQueue):
    web asks the server which watch events still wait
    if AI harness runs human ack <event>:
        stop showing message
        read the map of that file again

for each human file:
    web reads .json, human_<name>.json from human/human_<name>.json
    trees shows <folder>/<name>.human. if no folder, show in root folder



# HUMAN

if create file:
    the field file name opens empty 
    if name starts with / lands at the root
 
    if file name ends in .human:
        [refuse if bare name is already held by another human file or a file at the root](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:new_human)
        right-clicked folder path is kept in the map 
        
    file tree location is in the folder right clicked. if human: 
        real location is human/human_<name>.json
    
    [refuse if a path is out of the project, into human/, or onto a file already there](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:new_file). show reason. 
    [server makes the file empty](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the new file)

    new file is opened
  


  
if file compilation:
    stop if:
        file location is human/, 
        refusal happens and show in web the cli's message, file and location. 

    server receives request [as JSON](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:as JSON)

    for each abstraction text or code:
        if retext: run human retext --verbatim
        if new abstraction text: human map --verbatim
        if code: server writes code to file using python.
        if abstraction is deleted: 
            human undo <name> --entry <id>
            if another abstractions points to it, [refuse](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the gate)  
  
    if map has no abstractions, run logic as if no map.json exists.
    if expansion or create: [run human map --verbatim](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:compile_writing)
    
    [if windows, do not show terminal window](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:run_cli).
    send event if not:
        [code write is not pinned to an abstraction](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the pins that reach a file), 
        delete abstraction



if event appended to human/server/events.jsonl, the event includes:
    the kind, the name, the paths of the map and the file, the abstraction id
    the old text and the new
    if code edit: [the pins that reach the file](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the pins that reach a file).
    if abstraction expansion: the abstraction id that points to expansion, the highlighted words with their pins.
    if create: [the abstraction id it points to](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:compile_writing)

if human watch ran from project root:
    [prints once recommendation to no pipeline filter](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:cmd_watch),
    [prints once events not finished](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_watch) as one JSON line each,  
    if event printed before, [print event as "maybe_started":true](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:cmd_watch),
  
    continously prints the queue
    if --once: 
        prints once events waiting now and returns.


[ai harness takes them in order](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:The reader writes)
reads the diff of the abstraction text,
writes the code they ask for
if no file exists that does what abstraction asks:
    create a new file 
if abstraction no longer asks logic:
    removes the code

for each abstraction that points to the update abstraction or code:
    if the code was written for the abstraction text: run human sync  --for 
    if abstraction text edited: add pins using human retext

if [human ack <number>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_ack):
    the queue advances and prints how many events are left.



# SYNCRONIZATION

if code changes,
    run human sync <name>
    if folder name, refuse.
  
if human sync: 
    [deterministically](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:cmd_sync) [maps every old line to its new line](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the line map),
    [find again every pin and every span](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the re-resolving).  

    stop if:
        only lines moved,
        no abstraction holds the lines changed
        [--for abstraction id doesn't exist](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the entry the code was written for)

    if code written for the abstraction text
        run [human sync <name> --for <id>](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the entry that leaves)
    
    if lines changed, pin broken or new lines inside code block: find the abstractions that pins to the code
    
    send to ai compiler the request:
        the file absolute path to read the file
        the diff,
        [the imported files](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the line about the neighbours),
        the blocks,
        the abstractions to mend,
        explanation rules:
            to keep the untouched lines, 
            to keep every anchor, 
            ai compiler decides if modify abtraction text for each change
            if the abstraction [holds the user's words](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the mark on your words), do the smallest edit, in the user's text style.


[if human sync <human file>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:cmd_sync):
    if [--for id and abstraction id doesn't exist](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:written_for): stop
    use git head 
    [ask git for changed files since last commit](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:changed_files)

    [find again every file, block and abstraction pin](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:re_resolve)
    if a file, blok or pin doesn't exist: print

    [send one request to ai compiler](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:cmd_sync):
        if abstractions pins a changed file or a pin broke:
            the abstraction texts that pin to a changed file. [except abstraction <id> of --for, unless a pin of it broke](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:drop_written)
            [the diff of the changed files](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:the diff of the files a candidate pins), if no git old copy: show only the diff of the lines the pins reach
            [the pins that broke](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:the broken pins)
            for each --verbatim abstraction:
                append to request a mark
    
ai compiler:
    runs at the project root,
    receives request through the pipe
    if fails, stops and prints the reason ai compiler gave.
    [answers with the mended abstraction texts](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:ask_claude)

[copy the map and check the answer](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the rebuild), 

if check fails:
    try again up to --tries times. 4 by default
    if last time: leave the map untouched.

if every block, anchors other abstractions need, and pin targets exist: map gets saved
       
if code file and [new lines landed inside code block of an abstraction](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the pieces the new lines fall in) and abstraction didn't change:
    show warning
if [the sync moved --verbatim abstractions](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:the word when your words moved)
    show warning



## AN ABSTRACTION CHANGED OTHER ABSTRACTIONS

if [human sync <name> --stale <id>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_human.py:e1:repair_stale)
    stop if:
        abstraction id doesnt' exist
        [--for](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:written_for)
    repair and mark gets off. 

if sync, retext, repair changed abstraction 1's text and other human or code file abstractions point to it:
    each abstraction gets [marked as stale](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:mark_children)
    if abstraction 1 is in different file: add file path to note
    add abstraction 1 to the stale abstraction note list
    add abstraction 1 copy of the old text to its .json file.
    if other abstraction already stale, keeps its first old text.
    if other abstraction retexts, keep the stale mark

for each stale abstraction, send to ai compiler the request:
    abstraction 1 old text and new text
    diff between texts
    stale abstraction text,
    explanation rule:
        to mend the text that went wrong, 
        to keep every anchor and [every word other abstractions need](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:needed_words),
        ai compiler decides if to carry a new fact down at the stale abstraction's detail level, pinned at the abstraction 1's new anchor.
        if the stale abstraction holds the user's words, do the smallest edit, in the user's text style.
if abstraction 1 is gone, stop the run.

ai harness answers with the mended stale abstraction. text only, never code.
[check and save](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:repair_stale); 

if repair changed the user's abstraction text, print warning

for each abstraction that pointed to the staled abstraction:
    if abstraction text change: 
        [mark as stale](compiler/cli/human/compiler.py:e1:mark_children)
        each wait for its human sync --stale
